page: Amazon Web Services m7i.large is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture with 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core and 2 threads per core. The underlying processor is an Intel Xeon 8488C running at 3.2 GHz, equipped with 48 KB L1d cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 105 MB L3 cache. The instance is provisioned with 8.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance is average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 1845.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1747.0. However, multi-core and memory-bound workloads show limitations. The stress-ng multi-core score of 1895.08 and Geekbench multi-core score of 2133.0 are categorized as poor and weak, respectively. Memory bandwidth is also constrained, with uncached read speeds at 13.5 GB/sec and write speeds at 14.89 GB/sec.

The instance features advanced CPU instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for deep learning and cryptography acceleration. Despite these hardware capabilities, the resource density of 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB RAM limits its utility for heavy multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, or database operations, which score poorly in Passmark tests. Qualitatively, the m7i.large offers a cost-effective entry point for dedicated general-purpose workloads that require modern Intel instruction sets but do not demand high memory bandwidth or multi-core scaling. It is best suited for light web serving, text processing, and basic single-threaded applications.
